searches.note: Twenty seven searches of a share of twenty eight, one left unspent, none of them the author's. Sixteen were restricted to a house's own domain (lopezdeheredia.com five times, riojalta.com twice, marquesdemurrieta.com three times, cvne.com twice, bodegasmuga.com three times) and one to the Consejo Regulador's riojawine.com, and are read as primary through their summaries; the other ten went to the open web for second sources (founders' dates, the soil of Tondonia, the Hadid pavilion, the Ygay Blanco of 1986, the Eiffel hall, the Muga move and first vintage). No WebFetch was tried. Every record was tested; no fact that rests on no source was kept.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the houses' own pages for their own dates, vineyards and methods, then to the open web for the second source of each date and person, then to the Consejo's classification, which three label terms and two traps depend on.

Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source (the Montecillo estate, the Gran Reserva's barrel time, racking by gravity, the north west of Rioja Alta); where a detail could be found in no source or the sources disagreed, it was cut or said with less (Arequipa, the decade of the move to Ygay, the year of Murrieta's new winery, the ten years of keeping for Tondonia).

Sources whose title or address names a living person, or that are a writer's own site, were read in the results but never cited in the fragment or here; the fragment's own sources were left as the author wrote them.

tested: Founded 1877 (the library's year): the house's history page (the design and building of the complex began about 1877) and the Consejo's winery page: confirmed.

The station quarter: the house calls itself the oldest bodega in Haro and one of the first three in Rioja; a trade article of 2008 places it in the station quarter beside La Rioja Alta: the first bodega of the quarter is not the house's word, so changed to the oldest bodega in Haro, hedged as the house's account.

Viña Tondonia: on the right bank of the Ebro in a great meander, founded between 1913 and 1914, the first vines planted in 1913, named from Tondon, the old word for the meander (from the Latin retondo), on the house's vineyard and tour pages: confirmed.
The soil, alluvial clay with a high share of limestone: Grandi Bottiglie and a second merchant, with another account adding gravel and pebbles: confirmed.
The blend, about three quarters Tempranillo with Garnacho, Graciano and Mazuelo, all from the house's own vineyards (75, 15 and 10 per cent on the current page; 70, 20 and 10 for 2008): confirmed.

The making: fermentation in old oak vats kept by the house's coopers, with the yeasts of the skins and the vats and none added (the house's fermentation page and its Chinese brochure); six years in barrel, two rackings a year, fresh egg whites (the house's Reserva sheets); the barrels mostly of American oak and made by the house's own coopers: confirmed.
The Gran Reserva in others: the house's sheet gives nine years in barrel at the least, racked twice a year, not about ten: changed.
The keeping: the house's ten years and more was found on no page searched: cut, the line kept without a figure.

Zaha Hadid's pavilion, 2001 to 2006, enclosing a stand of the 1910 world fair that the house found in its outbuildings and restored: Zaha Hadid Architects and Archiweb: confirmed; Brussels is named in one account only and stays out. Zaha Hadid's dates, 1950 to 2016, are common record (Wikipedia, the firm's own pages).
The Reserva label term, at least three years with one in barrel: the Consejo's specification gives thirty six months, at least twelve in barrel and six in bottle: confirmed.
Serve 15 to 17 degrees Celsius: the house's sheets give 18 to 20; the record follows the Codex's reference for a medium red, as the author reported: kept.

The questions: one right answer each; the distractors of the cellar question are of one kind; the second question's Sierra de Cantabria lies north, above Rioja Alavesa, as its explanation says: sound.
The house rules: nobody living named (the family's present generation is in people.json and is not met in the record); no price, score or superlative; British; no dash: sound.

tested: Founded 1890 in Haro's station quarter as the Sociedad Vinícola de La Rioja Alta by five families of Rioja and the Basque Country: the house's history pages, its 2022 magazine and its Viña Ardanza post: confirmed.

The first president a woman: the house names her and calls her the first woman to preside over a commercial company in Spain: confirmed as the house's account; she stays described for want of her dates.
The first winemaker a Frenchman, who made the Reserva 1890 from which the 890 descends: the house's history: confirmed; he stays described.
The merger of 1904 with Bodegas Ardanza, owned by one of the founders, marked by the Reserva 1904 that became the 904: the house's history and its 2022 magazine: confirmed.
The year of the name La Rioja Alta (1891 or 1941 on the house's own pages): not in the record, as the author left it.

The 890 of 2011: Tempranillo 95 per cent, Graciano 3, Mazuelo 2; six years in barrel with ten rackings, bottled in July 2018; Tempranillo from old vines at Villalba, Briñas and Labastida and Graciano from the Montecillo estate at Fuenmayor: the house's 2011 sheet: the great majority confirmed, Montecillo changed.
Candlelight: the house's sheets for 2004 and 1985 give racking by candlelight: confirmed for the story's twentieth century.

The barrels: the house's own pages say its coopers make every barrel in its Haro cooperage from American oak air dried for two years; Enterwine dates the house's own barrel making to about 2002 and Spanish Wine Lover gives three years of drying: the claim is kept as the house's, and no longer carried through the twentieth century.
The Gran Reserva label term, at least five years with two in barrel and two in bottle: the Consejo's specification (sixty months, twenty four in barrel, twenty four in bottle): confirmed.
The questions: the number question has one right answer and four options of one kind; the station quarter question's explanation is right on López de Heredia (1877) and CVNE (1879): sound.
The house rules: nobody living named; no price, score or superlative in the record; British; no dash: sound.

changed.was: Old vineyards of the house near Haro: in its own sheets, Tempranillo from Villalba, Briñas and Labastida, with Graciano from its Montecillo vineyard.
changed.now: Vineyards of the house: in its sheet for the 2011 vintage, Tempranillo from old vines at Villalba, Briñas and Labastida near Haro, with Graciano from its Montecillo estate at Fuenmayor, west of Logroño.
changed.why: The house's 2011 sheet puts the Montecillo estate at Fuenmayor, some way east of Haro and west of Logroño, so near Haro was wrong for the Graciano; the sheet also says the sites are those of the 2011 vintage, since earlier sheets name other vineyards (Melchorón, Rodezno).

tested: Luciano de Murrieta, 1822 to 1911: Wikipedia's list of the marquesses and a burial record give both years; Noticias de Navarra and others give his death at Logroño in 1911 without heirs: confirmed.

Born in Arequipa: in Wikipedia and in an interview on the house's own site whose address names a living person; every other account says only Peru, and Noticias de Navarra gives him a Bolivian mother where the house's interview gives a Peruvian one: changed to born in Peru.

Bordeaux and 1852: the house's own pages (Rioja's first fine wine in 1852, made with methods learnt in Bordeaux, so that it would endure over time) and Noticias de Navarra: confirmed. His service with General Espartero and exile in London are in the house's interview only and stay out, as the author left them.

The cellars of the Duke of la Victoria at Logroño: not on the house's pages searched; Noticias de Navarra ties the property to the Duchess of la Victoria, Espartero's wife: kept on the author's two secondary accounts and left open.
The title of 1872: King Amadeo I, 20 October 1872, in Wikipedia's list; one account says Isabel II, who had left the throne in 1868: the record's the crown stands.
The move to Ygay: 1872 in one account, 1877 in another, 1852 in the house's interview: the decade is cut from the story.
1983, the Cebrián-Sagarriga family: the house's ethical code (run by the family since 1983) with the author's Wikipedia and Decanter: confirmed; the family name names no living person.

The castle and the new winery: the house's museum statement has a restoration of more than eight years ended in 2015 and the castle declared a museum in 2019; the house's About us gives the new winery in 2021, its sustainability page 2022: the museum kept as declared in 2019, the winery's year cut.

La Plana: the highest point of the Ygay estate at 485 metres, and Castillo Ygay always from it, on the house's own pages: confirmed (the house's Blanco page gives 485 metres for Capellanía too, not a contradiction of the red's site); its planting year (1950 or 1940) stays out, as the author left it.

The making of 2012: Tempranillo in American oak and Mazuelo in French oak, 34 months each, then 20 months in a concrete vat; blend 81 and 19 per cent; made only in exceptional years, with 2013 to 2015 not released: confirmed as written.
Castillo Ygay Blanco 1986: 252 months, twenty one years, in 225 litre American oak barrels and 67 months in concrete, bottled in January 2014 (MMD and Vinissimus, the house's sheet): confirmed.
The questions: Especial has one right answer; Bordeaux has one right answer and plausible distractors; the explanations teach: sound.
The house rules: nobody living named (the family's head is in people.json and is not named); no price or score (the house's pages carry scores and rankings, none taken); British; no dash: sound.

tested: Founded 1932 by Isaac Muga and Aurora Caño, a married couple, on the house's family page and the Consejo's winery page: confirmed; they stay described, since the founder's grandson of the same name is living.

The move to the Barrio de la Estación in 1970: Spanish Wine Lover and Astor Wines give 1970, Bound by Wine 1968 for a townhouse; the house's pages give no year, only a house about two hundred years old in the quarter: kept, left open. The house's first cellars under Haro's main street (Cellar Tours) are not in the record.
The first Prado Enea at the end of the 1960s: Decanter gives 1969 and bottles of 1969 are listed by Tastingbook and a merchant: confirmed.

The sites: the house's Prado Enea page gives the north west of Rioja Alta, the villages of Sajazarra, Cellorigo and Fonzaleche, 550 to 700 metres, calcareous clay and alluvial soils, high plots in the latest ripening zones, always the last grapes picked: north changed to north west, the soils added; the Montes Obarenes, on no house page, cut.
The blend, Tempranillo with Garnacha, Mazuelo and Graciano: Decanter and the house's page: confirmed.

The making: at least 36 months in oak casks and 36 in bottle (the house's Prado Enea page and Decanter): confirmed. The house's pages say racking by gravity and fining with egg whites: racked by hand changed to by gravity. Oak vats for the alcoholic fermentation of its Selección Especial and Prado Enea, wooden vats for Torre Muga and the Reserva: as every Muga red is, cut.
The house's coopers who build and mend its barrels and vats: the house's own questions page: confirmed.
Torre Muga, Tempranillo with Mazuelo and Graciano in French oak: the house's page: confirmed.
The name Prado Enea from a building once owned by a Dionisio de Prado: Decanter only, as the author found: stays out.
The questions: the making question has one right answer once the explanation speaks of Prado Enea; the year question's distractors are dated elsewhere in the group: sound.
The house rules: nobody living named (the founder's sons and grandsons are not named); no price or score (the house's news pages carry scores and rankings, none taken); British; no dash: sound.
